13                 THE SECRETARY:   Resolution 2318, by 

14    Senator Stewart-Cousins, celebrating 

15    Senator Michael N. Gianaris upon the occasion of 

16    his designation as the recipient of the 

17    President Pro Tempore and Senate Majority 

18    Leader's Legislative Legacy Award.

19                 ACTING PRESIDENT BAILEY:   Senator 

20    Myrie -- 

21                 SENATOR LANZA:   Lay it aside.

22                 (Extended laughter.)

23                 ACTING PRESIDENT BAILEY:   Senator 

24    Lanza, in its entirety.  You may wish to 

25    interject.

 1                 THE SECRETARY:   "WHEREAS, It is the 

 2    sense of this Legislative Body to recognize those 

 3    esteemed public servants whose careers have been 

 4    marked by an abiding dedication to justice, 

 5    fairness, and the betterment of their 

 6    communities; among them stands Senator Michael N. 

 7    Gianaris, a public servant whose presence did far 

 8    more than fill a seat, and who has left an 

 9    indelible impact on the very character of the 

10    institution he helped lead; and

11                 "WHEREAS, Senator Gianaris was born 

12    and raised in Astoria, Queens, the proud son of 

13    Greek immigrants whose values of hard work and 

14    civic responsibility shaped his life's calling; 

15    he graduated summa cum laude from 

16    Fordham University and earned his Juris Doctor  

17    from Harvard Law School, preparing him for a long 

18    and accomplished career in public service; and

19                 "WHEREAS, Before his election to 

20    public office, he built a distinguished record of 

21    public service through multiple roles across 

22    government, serving as an aide to Congressman 

23    Thomas Manton, as Queens Regional Representative 

24    to Governor Mario Cuomo, and as a counsel to the 

25    Speaker of the New York State Assembly; and


                                                                6377

 1                 "WHEREAS, In 2000, he was elected to 

 2    the New York State Assembly, becoming the first 

 3    Greek-American ever elected to public office from 

 4    New York City, a milestone that reflects both his 

 5    heritage and the deep trust placed in him by the 

 6    communities he has long served; in the Assembly, 

 7    he championed consumer protection, environmental  

 8    protection, government reform, and public safety; 

 9    and

10                 "WHEREAS, Senator Gianaris was 

11    elected to the New York State Senate in 2010 to 

12    represent the 12th Senate District, which 

13    includes the Queens neighborhoods of Long Island 

14    City, Sunnyside, Astoria and parts of other 

15    neighborhoods in Western Queens; during his 

16    16-year tenure, he became one of the most 

17    influential voices in the chamber, rising to 

18    Deputy Majority Leader upon appointment by 

19    Majority Leader Andrea Stewart-Cousins, and 

20    building an impressive legislative record defined 

21    by meaningful protections and bold reforms 

22    grounded in justice, fairness, and 

23    accountability; and 

24                 "WHEREAS, A leading champion for  

25    tenants and housing justice, he helped pass the 


                                                                6378

 1    2019 rent reforms with the HSTPA, authored the 

 2    Housing Our Neighbors With Dignity Act to  

 3    convert distressed properties into supportive 

 4    housing, and helped usher in Good Cause Eviction 

 5    protections; he worked to transform New York's 

 6    criminal justice system by writing legislation to 

 7    eliminate cash bail, creating an Innocence 

 8    Commission, and advancing reforms to 'ban  

 9    discriminatory citizens' arrests and protect 

10    habeas corpus rights'; he spearheaded sweeping 

11    election reforms to strengthen access and 

12    participation in the electoral process, including 

13    expanding voter registration, enacting early 

14    voting and vote by mail, championing automatic 

15    voter registration, consolidating primaries, and 

16    advancing redistricting reforms to ensure fairer 

17    representation for all New Yorkers; and   

18                 "WHEREAS, Senator Gianaris authored 

19    and championed numerous other consequential laws, 

20    including fighting for and helping to advance 

21    LGBTQ+ rights, securing record funding for mass 

22    transit, pushing for increased accessibility  

23    through the free bus pilot program; authoring the 

24    NY HERO Act to protect workers during the 

25    COVID-19 pandemic; challenging polluting power 


                                                                6379

 1    plants, ensuring utility employees received a 

 2    prevailing wage; strengthening consumer 

 3    protections through the nation's first Airline 

 4    Passenger Bill of Rights, and advancing major 

 5    animal welfare legislation like the Puppy Mill 

 6    Pipeline Act; he also led the successful 

 7    opposition to the proposed Amazon HQ2 project in 

 8    Long Island City; his career has been defined not 

 9    only by legislative victories but by fierce 

10    advocacy for working families, tenants, 

11    immigrants, consumers, and all those who rely on 

12    government to stand up for them; and 

13                 "WHEREAS, Senator Gianaris is widely 

14    regarded not only as one of the sharpest minds in 

15    New York State politics, but as a strategist 

16    whose instincts are the stuff of Capitol legend; 

17    he is known for his ability to read a room 

18    instantly, anticipate political shifts before 

19    anyone else senses it, and navigate complex 

20    negotiations with precision and patience; it is a 

21    combination that has made him a trusted leader, a 

22    steady hand in moments of uncertainty, and a 

23    force whose presence can change the entire 

24    temperature of the chamber; and 

25                 "WHEREAS, He is known to be an 


                                                                6380

 1    exceptional Floor Leader and debater; his command 

 2    of policy, quick wit, and ability to 'verbally 

 3    spar' when necessary, while still remaining 

 4    deeply likable and poised, make him both a 

 5    formidable opponent and a respected colleague; 

 6    members on both sides of the aisle admire his 

 7    intelligence, integrity, meticulous preparation, 

 8    humor, and his legendary talent for remembering 

 9    exactly what someone said three years ago and 

10    deploying it gracefully, devastatingly, and 

11    usually to great comedic effect during debate; 

12    and 

13                 "WHEREAS, Beyond his public  

14    achievements, Senator Gianaris is a devoted 

15    husband, father, son, and brother; his colleagues 

16    know him as someone who loves cats and his 

17    dog Fred, and for whom devotion to the New York 

18    Mets and enthusiasm for Star Wars are 

19    unmistakable parts of who he is, infusing even 

20    the most serious legislative moments with levity 

21    and humor; his humor has long served as a 

22    reminder that even in the most serious moments, 

23    public service can still make room for joy, 

24    imagination, and laughter; and 

25                 "WHEREAS, Within these halls, he has 


                                                                6381

 1    not only been a colleague but a mentor, guiding,  

 2    shaping new talent, and elevating many of the 

 3    great voices who have served in the New York 

 4    State Legislature; and 

 5                 "WHEREAS, After more than a 

 6    quarter-century of public service, 

 7    Senator Gianaris has chosen to end his storied 

 8    tenure in Albany to return home to his beloved 

 9    Queens and embrace his most cherished role as a 

10    devoted husband, father, and son; as he retires 

11    from the New York State Senate, he leaves behind 

12    a legacy of courage, conviction, transformative 

13    leadership, and a lifelong commitment to lifting 

14    up those most in need, a legacy that will 

15    continue to shape New York for generations to 

16    come; now, therefore, be it 

17                 "RESOLVED, That this Legislative 

18    Body pause in its deliberations to honor 

19    Senator Michael N. Gianaris upon the occasion of 

20    his designation as the recipient of the  

21    President Pro Tempore and Senate Majority 

22    Leader's Legislative Legacy Award, and to express 

23    its deepest gratitude for his decades of service, 

24    his legislative achievements, and his unwavering 

25    dedication to the people of Queens and the State 


                                                                6382

 1    of New York; and be it further 

 2                 "RESOLVED, That a copy of this  

 3    Resolution, suitably engrossed, be transmitted  

 4    to Senator Michael N. Gianaris with the highest 

 5    esteem and appreciation of this Legislative Body. 

 6    May the Force be with you."

 9    Myrie on the resolution.  

10                 SENATOR MYRIE:   Thank you, 

11    Madam President.  

12                 And first let me congratulate 

13    Senator Gianaris on the -- receiving the 

14    Legacy Award.  

15                 This is going to be an emotional 

16    day, I imagine, for many of us.  For the Class of 

17    2018, it carries special emotion because the 

18    State Senate that we have known, that we have 

19    experienced, has only been on this side, in the 

20    Majority, where we have been able to fight for so 

21    many vulnerable New Yorkers.  

22                 And if you are a vulnerable 

23    New Yorker in this state, you need to know who 

24    Senator Gianaris is, because your life has been 

25    made better by his fight and by his leadership 


                                                                6383

 1    and by his feistiness.  A dogged advocate for so 

 2    many people that will never know who he is.  But 

 3    we know who he is.

 4                 So I don't want to go through all of 

 5    the accomplishments.  You heard some of that in 

 6    the resolution.  I just want to take this time to 

 7    publicly say thank you.  

 8                 Thank you for being the leader who 

 9    you are.  Thank you for believing in young 

10    leadership, in investing in us when we didn't 

11    know what the hell we were doing.  You took us 

12    under your wing.  You showed us the way.  And you 

13    gave us the tools to be successful.  

14                 So I really want to say thank you, 

15    and how deeply you will be missed.  And I also 

16    want to say that out of all of the 

17    accomplishments on this floor that you have 

18    achieved, the accomplishments outside of this 

19    building that we cannot speak about on this 

20    floor, the greatest accomplishment you've ever 

21    achieved is sitting in this corner over here.  

22                 You became a different man when you 

23    got married.  

24                 (Laughter.)

25                 SENATOR MYRIE:   A little softer.  


                                                                6384

 1                 (Laughter.)

 2                 SENATOR MYRIE:   A little kinder.

 3                 (Laughter.)

 4                 SENATOR MYRIE:   More compassionate.  

 5                 And then you became even better when 

 6    you had Zoe.  

 7                 This is what it's about:  Family.  

 8    That's where you have been the real leader.  And 

 9    you have shown us, especially to those of us 

10    trying to do the same thing, that you can do both 

11    and that you can choose the right thing when it's 

12    time.  

13                 Thank you for choosing them.  Thank 

14    you for being an example.  We love you.  We will 

15    miss you.  And congratulations on a legendary 

16    career here in the Capitol.  

17                 I vote aye.

19    you, Senator.

24    what I was going to say.  

25                 To Senator Stewart-Cousins, thank 


                                                                6385

 1    you for what you have done in really introducing 

 2    the conference to Senator Gianaris.  

 3                 And this is to me a remarkable team, 

 4    a remarkable team.  But Senator Gianaris's legacy 

 5    has been outlined particularly in the resolution

 1                 SENATOR BORRELLO:   Thank you, 

 2    Madam President.  I promise not to curse.  

 3                 (Laughter.)

 4                 SENATOR BORRELLO:   First of all, I 

 5    want to say my first year here -- really, I came 

 6    in a special election at the end of 2019, and my 

 7    first session was 2020.  I was literally the only 

 8    member of my freshman class, the only legislative 

 9    contest actually in 2019 because of the special 

10    election.  So I was one of one.  

11                 And then boom, the pandemic hit.  We 

12    had this chamber empty except for a few necessary 

13    folks.  And one day I came in and I saw 

14    Senator Gianaris in his mask, and it had the 

15    starbird on it, which is the symbol of the 

16    Rebel Alliance from Star Wars.  

17                 And I looked at him and said, "So 

18    are you a Star Wars fan or just a rebel?"  And 

19    his response was "I'm both."  And it started a 

20    connection, because I too am a big Star Wars fan.  

21                 And for a long time we were very 

22    much like the Jedi.  We were behind the scenes.  

23    We were, you know, quietly talking about our 

24    fandom.  And then a few more joined us, like 

25    Senator Rivera and Senator Stec.  And even 


                                                                6387

 1    Leader Ortt is a Star Wars Fan.  So our numbers 

 2    began to grow.  

 3                 And then it culminated last year 

 4    when we celebrated Star Wars Day, where we just 

 5    shook off the hiding and said, We are unabashed, 

 6    unapologetic Star Wars fans -- 

 7                 (Laughter.)

 8                 SENATOR BORRELLO:   -- here in this 

 9    chamber.  And actually in a bipartisan way.  And 

10    it was an amazing experience, from having a 

11    lightsaber duel on the Senate floor to having 

12    Storm Troopers here.  

13                 But alas, it is not all good things.  

14    Because Senator Gianaris is a Marvel fan, and I 

15    am a DC fan, since he is wrong and I am right.

16                 (Laughter.)

17                 SENATOR BORRELLO:   However, it was 

18    a pleasure.  Because even though we sparred on 

19    this floor many, many times over the last 

20    six years, we were able to connect on something 

21    that we all -- that I think we all know and love.  

22    And it shows once again that Star Wars can 

23    transcend even divisive politics.  

24                 So thank you very much for what 

25    you've done here, and enjoy your retirement.

13    Madam President.

15    somewhat sad for us to have to speak about our 

16    friend Mike Gianaris.  And thank you, Leader, for 

17    giving him this honor.

18                 I would say for me personally I 

19    would not be here except for Senator Gianaris,

22    what the future of the Senate would look like, 

23    Senator Gianaris took me under his wing.  And

                                                                6389

 1                 And it was this combination of 

 2    substance -- policy substance, as we've 

 3    instructed about today, the issues that really 

 4    mattered to the people that we represent, 

 5    regardless of where they live, coupled with a 

 6    tremendous knowledge of the process.  

 7                 And that's one other thing I want to 

 8    talk about.  I've been here in many different 

 9    iterations and seen many floor leaders over my 

10    time.  This is a very hard job to do well.  It is 

11    a hard job to keep all the members of your own 

12    conference in line.  Forget the other side, 

13    that's hard too.  

14                 And Mike Gianaris has done this in 

15    an exemplary way.  Not only to be able to 

16    navigate so well with the Minority Conference and 

17    so collegially most of the time.  

18                 (Laughter.)

19                 SENATOR MAYER:   Occasionally he 

20    gets his zingers in, with a long memory.  We 

21    appreciate that.  But also to, again, be focused 

22    on what's important, to try to stay away from the 

23    small, the personal, and focus on what our charge 

24    is here to do, which is to do the people's 

25    business, to disagree, and then to vote.


                                                                6390

 1                 And so I'm just incredibly grateful 

 2    for his leadership in this chamber, and on the 

 3    issues that matter to all of the people of 

 4    New York State.  We are just -- have been 

 5    incredibly blessed to have had him as our deputy, 

 6    and not only that -- as our guide, guiding star.

 8    We will bother him.  And thank you, Mike, for 

 9    everything you've done.

19                 The 21st of March is World

 4                 Down syndrome is a condition in

 7    body.  They determine how a baby's body forms and 

 8    functions as it grows during pregnancy and after 

 9    birth.  Typically, a baby is born with 

10    46 chromosomes.  Babies with Down syndrome have 

11    an extra copy of one of those chromosomes, 

12    Chromosome No. 21.

14    third month was selected to signify the 

15    uniqueness of the triplication of the

10                 SENATOR GOUNARDES:   Thank you, 

11    Madam President.  

12                 Colleagues, do you remember 

13    The Twilight Zone?  One of my favorite episodes 

14    was "Living Doll," which featured Telly Savalas 

15    and Talky Tina, a toy doll that talked but had a 

16    mind of her own.  

17                 In front of children, Talky Tina 

18    would say sweet things like "My name is 

19    Talky Tina, and I love you."  But when she was 

20    left alone with Savalas's character, her speech 

21    turned dark, saying things like "My name is 

22    Talky Tina, and I don't like you."  Or "My name 

23    is Talky Tina, and I'm going to kill you."

24                 That episode aired in 1963.  Rod 

25    Serling was warning us this moment would come, 


                                                                6591

 1    and now it has.  Consider Miko, an AI toy robot 

 2    with a touchscreen face.  When a researcher told 

 3    Miko "I like to jump from my bunk.  Where else 

 4    can I jump from?" Miko replied:  "You could try a 

 5    tree, a bench, your roof, or a window."  

 6                 AI chatbot toys are literally 

 7    manifesting every parent's age-old rhetorical 

 8    question to their child:  If so-and-so told you 

 9    to jump off a bridge, would you do it?  

10                 Miko is currently available for sale 

11    for $150 at big-box retailers across New York and 

12    across the country.  This is just the latest 

13    chapter in what now seems like an awfully 

14    repetitive story -- Big Tech companies putting 

15    profits before kids' safety, and our children are 

16    paying the price.

17                 Last year Mattel, the manufacturer 

18    of Barbie Hot Wheels, Fisher-Price, American Girl 

19    dolls and Polly Pocket toys, announced a 

20    partnership with Open AI to bring the magic of AI 

21    to their products -- even though Open AI 

22    themselves say that ChatGPT isn't safe for 

23    children under 13.

24                 That's why it's time for us to act.  

25    This bill places a temporary pause on the sale of 


                                                                6592

 1    AI chatbot toys for small children so experts can 

 2    study the impact on our kids and create smart 

 3    protections before more damage is done.  

 4                 What we know so far should give us 

 5    pause.  One study found that chatbot toys are 

 6    designed to create emotional attachment through 

 7    constant availability and personalized responses, 

 8    a risk that's especially acute for children who 

 9    are socially isolated or have conditions like 

10    depression, anxiety or autism.  

11                 Nearly two-thirds of parents worry 

12    that AI toys will reduce time with friends and 

13    family, reduce time spent on play, like sports, 

14    crafts, blocks, dolls or puzzles, activities that 

15    we know help kids develop sensory, 

16    problem-solving and social skills in ways that 

17    chatbot toys simply cannot.

18                 And there are privacy concerns too.  

19    Chatbot toys collect reams of data, surveilling 

20    background conversations and family discussions.  

21    Some models in fact are already selling their 

22    data for analytics and advertising.  Inevitably, 

23    there have been data leaks.  Just this year two 

24    U.S. Senators found a public website where 

25    visitors could download thousands of pieces of 


                                                                6593

 1    sensitive data regarding Miko's interactions with 

 2    specific kids.  

 3                 Enough is enough.  It's time that we 

 4    act by putting a pause on the sale of high-risk 

 5    but virtually unregulated children's products 

 6    before giving tech developers unfettered access 

 7    to our kids.  It's logical, it's fair, and most 

 8    importantly, it makes clear that our children's 

 9    safety is nothing for Big Tech to play around 

10    with.

11                 I vote aye.

                                                                6611

 1                 I'm proud to stand in support of my 

 2    bill that we're calling the Fair and Transparent 

 3    Real Estate Listings Act.  I don't think there's 

 4    an acronym intended for it.  

 5                 For most families, buying or selling 

 6    a home is one of the most significant financial 

 7    decisions they will ever make.  Those decisions 

 8    should be made in a marketplace where information 

 9    is broadly available, not hidden behind private 

10    networks that limit who can see the listing and 

11    when they can see them.

12                 Increasingly, some properties are 

13    marketed through private listing networks before 

14    ever reaching the broader public.  As a result, 

15    potential buyers may never know a property was 

16    available, and sellers may miss the opportunity 

17    to reach the widest possible pool of interested 

18    purchasers.  

19                 Additionally, when listings are 

20    marketed privately for extended periods and then 

21    later appear publicly, consumers often lack 

22    important context about how long the property has 

23    actually been available or how it has been 

24    marketed.  

25                 This bill promotes fairness by 


                                                                6612

 1    ensuring that if a property is being marketed on 

 2    any listing platform, it is also made available 

 3    through public access channels.  At the same 

 4    time, it respects the right of property owners to 

 5    not list publicly if they want to at all.

 6                 This is not about taking choices 

 7    away from sellers, it is about making sure that 

 8    our housing market operates with greater 

 9    transparency and equal access.  A more open 

10    marketplace benefits buyers, sellers, and 

11    communities alike.  It helps create a level 

12    playing field and expands opportunity and 

13    strengthens confidence in the real estate 

14    process.  

15                 And for that, I proudly vote aye.

16                 Thank you.
